description:
A gate using the `label_target_validation` checker reports a configuration fault for every target label holding a short id, which is the form the planning-bracket template writes. Breakdown nodes in adopting repositories cannot pass such a gate, so their containers cannot be released.

## Background

The planning-bracket template labels a breakdown node `brackets:{container.short_id}`, and adopter documentation declares that form. The checker read the label value as a full issue id and compared it for equality, so `brackets:55c3e433` fails with "Issue not found: 55c3e433" although that issue exists and validates. The comparison arrived in commit `90439e25c`, when executor families moved to already-resolved issue ids. That change is correct for command arguments; a label value is unresolved input. It replaced a prefix resolution with an equality test, and the suite only exercised full-id labels, so nothing caught it. The defect reached gf2 on breakdown `228c4691`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A target label holding a unique short id validates the issue it names and returns that issue's verdict.
- [hard] REQ-02: Target resolution goes through the shared issue-id prefix resolver, so unknown and ambiguous targets yield its typed errors as fault runs, with the offending label named in the message.
- [hard] REQ-03: The checker reference states that a target may be a full id or a unique prefix.
title: Resolve short-id targets in label target validation
